questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.question: A legume folds its leaflets at night and reopens them during daylight without bending toward the light source. What is this sleep movement called?
questions.explanation: Nyctinasty is a reversible nastic sleep movement associated with the day-night cycle and is not oriented by stimulus direction.
optionExplanations: Phototropism is directional growth toward/away from light.
Correct. Nyctinasty is the classic plant sleep movement.
Geotropism is directional growth in response to gravity.
Hydrotropism is directional growth in response to water.
questions.sourceTag: 2023 recalled topic signal + Sir Brian mock-focus baseline 2026-10-09

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.question: A corn crop shows uniform yellowing that starts on the older leaves while the newest leaves remain greener. Which nutrient is most likely deficient?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is mobile in plants, so deficiency symptoms typically begin on older leaves as general chlorosis.
optionExplanations: Correct. Mobile N is remobilized to younger tissues.
Iron deficiency generally appears first on young leaves.
Calcium deficiency affects growing points and young tissues.
Boron deficiency commonly damages meristems and young tissues.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.question: Which symptom is most characteristic of potassium deficiency in many field crops?
options: Marginal yellowing and scorching beginning on older leaves
Interveinal chlorosis only on the youngest leaves
Death of the shoot tip before leaf symptoms
White powdery fungal growth on leaf surfaces
questions.explanation: Potassium is mobile and deficiency often begins on older leaves with marginal chlorosis that progresses to necrosis or scorching.
optionExplanations: Correct. Marginal scorch on older leaves is classic.
This more strongly suggests iron deficiency.
Growing-point death is more typical of calcium or boron deficiency.
Powdery growth indicates disease, not nutrient deficiency.
questions.sourceTag: 2023 recalled topic signal + Sir Brian mock-focus baseline 2026-10-09

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.question: Why do deficiencies of mobile nutrients such as nitrogen and magnesium often appear first on older leaves?
options: The plant can retranslocate them from old tissues to actively growing tissues
Young leaves have no vascular connections
Mobile nutrients are not used in growing tissues
questions.explanation: Mobile nutrients can be remobilized from older leaves to younger growing organs, causing older leaves to show deficiency first.
optionExplanations: Correct. Remobilization explains the symptom pattern.
Water supply is not the defining reason.
Growing tissues have strong nutrient demand.
questions.sourceTag: 2023 recalled topic signal + Sir Brian mock-focus baseline 2026-10-09
